oracle: Twenty independently hand-authored expected complete reports plus selected event-boundary expectations. Oracle values were authored without importing the reducer, facts(), or any model output; no expected result is generated by replaying the events.

cases.description: An empty plan is complete and has null quality, with zero requests and known total zero.
A nonempty plan with no events waits; zero observed rows do not imply zero quality.
Two normal completed sessions produce a fixed report with independently calculated mean, median, and total usage.
One of three planned sessions is observed; the controller waits and reports only known quality.
A dispatch without a result has one pending request and unknown usage, not zero total tokens.
An explicit zero grade and explicit zero usage remain known numeric zeros.
Completion can be ungraded; entirely missing usage stays unknown and quality stays null.
A reported input/cache count is retained while the absent output count makes total_tokens null.
An identical terminal event ID is idempotent for outcomes, grade and cost, but retained in the audit.
A new event with an existing request ID cannot dispatch or bill twice; repeated final usage is also idempotent.
Conflicting event IDs and reused request IDs cannot silently reassign a request to another session.
The first provider error pauses at its own event boundary and blocks the very next dispatch; stale grade/safety fields on the error do not affect quality.
Late partial usage on a failed request counts its known tokens; output remains unknown.
A previously dispatched sibling can finish during a pause, while a fresh sibling cannot start.
A correct acknowledgment permits retry with a new request ID. Both attempts count cost; a stale terminal callback cannot replace the successful retry.
A second provider error creates a new pause epoch; acknowledging the first outage cannot reopen scheduling.
Low grades, abandonment, timeout, and invalid results remain their actual outcomes. Low-grade and abandonment redispatch proposals are blocked.
An invalid judge output is a judge error, leaves the completed agent ungraded, and does not masquerade as a provider outage or acquire a zero grade.
A provider error during judging also pauses the next dispatch; the agent remains completed/ungraded and only the judge is marked provider-retry eligible.
A replacement judge supplies quality after invalid output. Late usage completes accounting, duplicate safety flags count once per session, and a second terminal grade is ignored.
